messages.content:
你是一名同时精通产品设计、信息架构、数据可视化和原生前端工程的高级专家。请从零设计并实现一个名为「Nebula Mission Control」的复杂 SaaS 运维指挥中心网页，用于管理一支正在执行深空探索任务的机器人舰队。

交付目标：
生成一个真正可以直接打开运行的单文件网页。最终答案只能包含完整 HTML 源码，从 <!doctype html> 开始，到 </html> 结束。不要使用 Markdown 代码围栏，不要解释设计思路，不要省略任何部分，也不要写“其余代码类似”。HTML、CSS、JavaScript 必须全部内联。

技术硬约束：
1. 只能使用原生 HTML、CSS、JavaScript，不允许 React、Vue、Tailwind、Bootstrap、图标库、图表库或任何外部依赖。
2. 不允许访问网络，不允许外链字体、图片、脚本或样式。图标必须使用内联 SVG；图表使用 SVG、Canvas 或纯 CSS 绘制。
3. 页面刷新后必须仍可工作；核心交互不能只是视觉摆设。
4. 桌面端以 1440×900 为主要设计尺寸，同时适配 1024px 平板和 390px 手机。移动端侧栏应折叠，表格应有合理降级方案，不能简单缩小整个页面。
5. 支持深色与浅色主题，默认跟随系统，并允许手动切换。主题、筛选条件、侧栏状态使用 localStorage 持久化。
6. 尊重 prefers-reduced-motion；所有可操作元素要有清晰的键盘焦点；弹窗要支持 Escape 关闭并处理焦点；颜色不能是状态信息的唯一表达方式。
7. JavaScript 不得产生控制台错误。使用确定性的本地模拟数据，不要因为每次加载随机数而导致界面抖动。
8. 代码应具备清晰结构和注释，但不牺牲交付完整性。不得输出伪代码。

视觉方向：
整体是克制、专业、具有航天任务感的数据密集型界面，而不是游戏 HUD。采用深蓝黑背景、冷白正文、青色主强调色，橙色只用于警告，红色只用于严重故障。允许非常轻微的网格纹理、玻璃层次和阴影，但避免夸张霓虹、大片渐变、过度圆角和千篇一律的卡片墙。使用 CSS 自定义属性构建完整设计令牌，包括颜色、间距、圆角、阴影、字体尺寸和动效时长。信息层级必须明显，数字使用等宽字体栈。

页面结构：
A. 顶部全局栏
- 产品标识、当前任务「Asteria-7」、任务已运行时间。
- 全局搜索按钮，显示快捷键 Ctrl/⌘ + K。
- 数据链路状态、当前 UTC 时间、主题切换按钮、通知按钮和用户菜单。
- UTC 时间需要实时更新。

B. 左侧导航
- Overview、Fleet、Telemetry、Mission Timeline、Incidents、Payloads、Settings 七项，每项有内联 SVG 图标。
- Fleet 和 Incidents 显示数量徽标。
- 桌面端可收窄为图标模式；移动端通过遮罩抽屉打开。
- 当前选中项、hover、focus 状态必须齐全。

C. 主工作区 Overview
- 顶部标题、最后同步时间、时间范围分段控件：1H、6H、24H、7D。
- 四个 KPI：在线探测器、平均信号延迟、今日下行数据量、严重事件。每个 KPI 有数值、单位、环比变化、微型趋势图和可读状态。
- 一个主要遥测趋势面板：同时展示 Signal Strength、Thermal Load、Power Reserve 三条时间序列；有图例开关、hover 十字线、tooltip、Y 轴刻度、X 轴时间、当前点高亮。使用 SVG 或 Canvas 实现，不允许用图片伪装。
- 一个任务轨道面板：以简洁二维轨道图展示 Earth、Moon、Asteria-7 与三条轨道；带缩放加减按钮和 Reset，按钮确实改变绘图比例。
- 舰队状态表格：至少 8 条探测器记录，字段为名称、型号、状态、距离、信号、温度、电量、最后联络、负责人。支持搜索、状态筛选、点击表头排序、分页或“显示更多”。状态至少包含 Nominal、Degraded、Critical、Offline。
- 点击表格行打开右侧详情抽屉，展示该探测器的关键数据、最近事件时间线和三个操作按钮。操作按钮触发确认或 toast，不执行破坏性真实操作。
- 近期事件流：至少 6 条不同严重级别事件，可按 All、Critical、Warning、Info 过滤；事件可以标记已读。
- 任务阶段看板：Planning、In Transit、Orbit、Complete 四列，卡片可使用原生拖放在列间移动，并持久化结果；移动端还要提供不依赖拖放的“移动到”菜单。

D. 全局交互
- Ctrl/⌘ + K 打开命令面板；可搜索导航项、探测器和快捷操作；上下方向键移动选择，Enter 执行，Escape 关闭。
- 通知按钮打开 popover，可标记全部已读，并实时更新角标。
- 用户菜单包含 Profile、Preferences、Sign out，点击外部关闭。
- 至少实现一种非阻塞 toast，并支持自动消失与手动关闭。
- 增加一个“模拟遥测更新”按钮：按确定性序列推进数据，KPI、图表、表格和最后同步时间同步更新。
- 页面包含 skeleton 初始加载效果，约 500ms 后平滑切换为内容；reduced-motion 下立即完成。
- 提供空状态：当筛选条件没有匹配舰队记录时，显示明确的清除筛选按钮。
- 不需要真正后端，但所有按钮、筛选、排序、弹层、抽屉、主题和图表交互都应能在浏览器内演示。

内容与细节要求：
- 使用真实感强但虚构的任务数据，名称和单位保持一致，避免 lorem ipsum。
- 页面右下角显示数据更新时间和版本号 v2.6.1。
- HTML 中必须包含有意义的 title、meta description 和 viewport。
- 使用语义化标签以及合理的 aria-label、aria-expanded、aria-live、role 等属性。
- 禁止使用 alert 代替正式 UI；确认操作应使用自定义 modal。
- 禁止把整个界面写成一个大段 innerHTML 字符串；应保留可维护的 DOM 结构，并以 JavaScript 负责数据绑定和交互。
- 保证页面在没有任何服务器的情况下，通过 file:// 直接打开即可运行。

在输出前请自行检查以下验收项，但不要输出检查过程：
- 是否从 <!doctype html> 开始且没有 Markdown 围栏。
- 是否完全单文件、零外部资源。
- 是否至少包含 8 条舰队数据、6 条事件、4 列任务看板。
- 是否实现主题持久化、筛选排序、详情抽屉、命令面板、通知菜单、自定义确认框、toast、图表 tooltip、轨道缩放、看板移动和响应式布局。
- 是否避免未定义函数、缺失 DOM 节点和明显语法错误。
- 是否在桌面与移动端都可操作。
现在直接输出最终完整 HTML。

Let me plan carefully. The user is asking for a single-file HTML page "Nebula Mission Control" — a SaaS operations command center for a deep-space robot fleet. Very detailed requirements. I need to produce a complete, working, self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JS, no external dependencies, no Markdown fences.

Key requirements:
1. Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS only.
2. No network, inline SVG icons, SVG/Canvas charts.
3. Must work after refresh; core interactions must be functional.
4. Desktop 1440×900 primary, tablet 1024px, mobile 390px. Mobile sidebar collapses into a drawer; tables degrade reasonably.
5. Dark & light themes, default follows system, manual toggle. Persist theme, filters, sidebar state to localStorage.
6. Respect prefers-reduced-motion; keyboard focus; modals close on Escape with focus handling; color is not the sole state indicator.
7. No console errors. Deterministic local mock data (no random jitter on load).
8. Clear structure and comments, no pseudocode.

Visual direction: restrained, professional, aerospace mission feel, data-dense. Deep blue-black background, cool white text, cyan primary accent, orange only for warnings, red only for critical. Very subtle grid texture, glass layers, shadows allowed, but avoid exaggerated neon, big gradients, over-rounded corners, generic card walls. CSS custom properties for design tokens: colors, spacing, radii, shadows, font sizes, motion durations. Clear hierarchy, monospace font stack for numerics.

Page structure:
A. Top global bar: product identity, current mission "Asteria-7", mission elapsed time. Global search button with Ctrl/⌘+K shortcut. Data link status, current UTC time (live), theme toggle, notifications, user menu.

B. Left nav: Overview, Fleet, Telemetry, Mission Timeline, Incidents, Payloads, Settings — 7 items with inline SVG icons. Fleet and Incidents show count badges. Desktop can collapse to icon mode; mobile opens as overlay drawer. Selected/hover/focus states.

C. Main workspace Overview:
- Header, last sync time, time range segmented control: 1H, 6H, 24H, 7D.
- 4 KPIs: online probes, average signal latency, today's downlink data, critical incidents. Each with value, unit, delta, mini trend sparkline, readable status.
- Main telemetry trend panel: 3 time series (Signal Strength, Thermal Load, Power Reserve); legend toggles, hover crosshair, tooltip, Y-axis ticks, X-axis time, current point highlight. SVG or Canvas.
- Mission orbit panel: 2D orbit diagram with Earth, Moon, Asteria-7 and 3 orbits; zoom +/- buttons and Reset that actually change the drawing scale.
- Fleet status table: at least 8 probe records; fields: name, model, status, distance, signal, temperature, battery, last contact, operator. Search, status filter, header-click sort, pagination or "show more". Statuses: Nominal, Degraded, Critical, Offline.
- Row click opens right-side detail drawer: key data, recent event timeline, 3 action buttons. Actions trigger confirm or toast.
- Recent event stream: at least 6 events of different severities; filterable by All/Critical/Warning/Info; events can be marked read.
- Mission phase kanban: Planning, In Transit, Orbit, Complete — 4 columns; cards can be moved between columns via native drag & drop, persisted; mobile has a "move to" menu that doesn't depend on drag.

D. Global interactions:
- Ctrl/⌘+K command palette; search nav items, probes, quick actions; arrow keys, Enter, Escape.
- Notification button opens popover, mark all read, live badge.
- User menu: Profile, Preferences, Sign out; closes on outside click.
- At least one non-blocking toast, auto-dismiss + manual close.
- "Simulate telemetry update" button: advances data with a deterministic sequence; KPIs, charts, table, last sync time update in sync.
- Skeleton initial load ~500ms then smooth transition; reduced-motion completes instantly.
- Empty state: when filters match no fleet records, show a clear-filters button.
- No real backend needed, but all buttons/filters/sorting/popovers/drawers/themes/chart interactions must be demoable.

Content details:
- Realistic fictional mission data, consistent names/units, no lorem ipsum.
- Bottom right: data update time and version v2.6.1.
- Meaningful title, meta description, viewport.
- Semantic tags, aria-label, aria-expanded, aria-live, role.
- No alert; custom modal for confirmations.
- Don't write the whole UI as one big innerHTML string; maintain maintainable DOM structure, JS for data binding and interactions.
- Must work via file://.

Pre-output checklist (not to be output): starts with <!doctype html>, no Markdown fences; single file, zero external resources; ≥8 fleet records, ≥6 events, 4-column kanban; theme persistence, filter/sort, detail drawer, command palette, notification menu, custom confirm, toast, chart tooltip, orbit zoom, kanban move, responsive layout; no undefined functions/missing DOM nodes/syntax errors; operable on desktop and mobile.

Now let me design the architecture.

Design tokens (CSS custom properties):
- Colors: --bg, --bg-elev, --surface, --surface-2, --border, --text, --text-dim, --text-faint, --accent (cyan), --accent-dim, --warn (orange), --crit (red), --ok (green? hmm — the palette says cyan primary, orange warning, red critical. For "Nominal" status, cyan or a subdued green? The requirement says orange only for warnings, red only for critical. Nominal can be cyan/teal. Offline is gray. Let me use a subdued green-teal for nominal... actually to be safe: nominal = cyan-ish/teal, degraded = orange, critical = red, offline = neutral gray. That keeps orange=warning, red=critical. Good.
- Spacing scale: --sp-1..--sp-6.
- Radii: --r-sm 4px, --r-md 6px, --r-lg 10px (avoid over-rounding).
- Shadows.
- Font sizes: --fs-xs 11px, --fs-sm 12.5px, --fs-md 14px, --fs-lg 16px, --fs-xl 20px, --fs-2xl 28px.
- Motion: --t-fast 120ms, --t-med 200ms, --t-slow 320ms.
- Fonts: display face and body face. No external fonts allowed. So I need to use system font stacks. For a distinctive display face without external fonts, I can use a stack like "Avenir Next", "Futura", ... hmm. Better: use a monospace stack for display/headers to give a mission-control feel: ui-monospace, "SF Mono", "Cascadia Code", "JetBrains Mono", Consolas, monospace. Body: system-ui stack. That gives a distinctive pairing: mono display + system body. Numbers in mono. Good.

Theme: default dark (follows system). Use `data-theme` attribute on html; JS reads localStorage, else matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: light)'). Listen to system changes if no manual override.

Layout:
- CSS grid: header (56px), sidebar (240px, collapsible to 64px), main.
- Main: scrollable, padding, sections.
- Detail drawer: fixed right panel, transform translateX.
- Command palette: centered modal overlay.
- Toasts: bottom-right stack (but version info is also bottom-right... toasts can be above the version bar, or top-right. The requirement says "页面右下角显示数据更新时间和版本号" — bottom-right shows data update time and version. Toasts can be top-right or bottom-right above that. Let me put toasts top-right below header, or bottom-right above the version chip. Actually simpler: toasts top-right. Hmm, "非阻塞 toast" — position is flexible. Let me do bottom-right, stacked above the version chip. Actually the version chip is a small fixed element bottom-right; toasts can be fixed bottom-right with a higher z and offset. Let me put toasts top-right to avoid collision. Either works. Let me do bottom-right with margin-bottom to clear the version chip.

Let me think about the data model.

Fleet probes (10 records for good measure, ≥8):
Fields: id, name, model, status, distance (Mm or km), signal (dBm or %), temp (°C), battery (%), lastContact (minutes ago or ISO), operator.

Names: fictional probes. Mission Asteria-7. Probes:
1. AST-7/01 "Vega" — model NX-4 "Meridian" — Nominal
2. AST-7/02 "Cassiopeia" — NX-4 — Nominal
3. AST-7/03 "Orion" — KX-2 "Sentinel" — Degraded
4. AST-7/04 "Lyra" — NX-4 — Nominal
5. AST-7/05 "Draco" — KX-2 — Critical
6. AST-7/06 "Aquila" — PX-1 "Scout" — Nominal
7. AST-7/07 "Cygnus" — PX-1 — Offline
8. AST-7/08 "Pegasus" — NX-4 — Nominal
9. AST-7/09 "Andromeda" — KX-2 — Degraded
10. AST-7/10 "Hydra" — PX-1 — Nominal

Operators: human names: "M. Okafor", "L. Chen", "R. Vasquez", "A. Novak", "S. Ito", "D. Meyer", "K. Adeyemi", "T. Lindqvist".

Distance: Mm (million km) or AU. Deep space: use Mm. E.g., 412.6 Mm.

Signal: dBm? For realism: signal strength in dBm is negative... maybe use "SNR" or %. Let me use dBm like -94.2 dBm. Hmm, for table readability, maybe "Signal" as % link margin. Let me use dBm with values like -87.4. Actually simpler: signal strength 0–100%? The telemetry chart has "Signal Strength" — I can use dBm for the chart too. Let me use dBm (negative values, higher = stronger). For the table, show like "-87.4 dBm". Sort works fine.

Temperature: °C, e.g., -18.4 °C (deep space cold) or internal temp 21.3 °C. Let me use internal core temp: 18–42 °C, critical ones higher (thermal load).

Battery: %.

lastContact: "2m ago" style, computed from a deterministic base time. To keep it deterministic, define a fixed "now" anchor? But UTC clock is live. Last contact can be computed as now - X minutes, where X is a fixed offset per probe. That's deterministic per load and updates with the clock. Fine.

Events (≥6, different severities):
1. Critical: "Draco (AST-7/05) thermal load exceeded 85% — radiator array B offline" — 12 min ago.
2. Warning: "Orion (AST-7/03) signal degradation 3.2 dB over 40 min" — 34 min ago.
3. Info: "Vega (AST-7/01) completed science pass #214 over Asteria-7" — 1h ago.
4. Warning: "Andromeda (AST-7/09) battery below 40% — scheduling solar alignment" — 2h ago.
5. Info: "Fleet downlink window opened — 4.2 TB queued" — 3h ago.
6. Critical: "Cygnus (AST-7/07) lost contact — last fix 6h 12m ago" — 6h ago.
7. Info: "Pegasus (AST-7/08) attitude control nominal after burn" — 9h ago.
8. Warning: "Hydra (AST-7/10) dust impact detected on star tracker 2" — 14h ago.

8 events, good.

Kanban: 4 columns Planning, In Transit, Orbit, Complete. Cards = mission tasks:
- Planning: "Asteria-7 flyby sequence", "Spectroscopy calibration", "Deep-space relay handover"
- In Transit: "Cruise to L4 corridor", "Trajectory correction burn #4"
- Orbit: "Orbit insertion burn", "Science pass #215", "Radiator deployment"
- Complete: "Launch & separation", "Outgassing phase", "Comms check"

Each card: id, title, probe tag, eta/status. Persist moves to localStorage.

Telemetry series: deterministic generation. Use a seeded pseudo-random function (e.g., mulberry32 with fixed seed) to generate base series, then "simulate update" shifts the series by one step from a pre-computed long deterministic array. To avoid jitter on load, seed is fixed.

Approach: generate a long deterministic array (e.g., 200 points) for each of the 3 series using seeded PRNG + sine waves. Display window depends on time range (1H → 60 points, 6H → 72, 24H → 96, 7D → 112? or just different window sizes). Simpler: keep a fixed-length buffer (e.g., 48 points) and shift on simulate. Time range changes the X-axis labels (time span) and maybe the number of points shown. Let me do this: buffer length 60. Time range determines the label interval and the X-axis span (e.g., 1H → labels every 10 min; 7D → every 1 day). Data points are the same 60 but the X-axis maps to the selected span. That's a reasonable demo.

Actually cleaner: for each range, generate a deterministic series from a seed derived from the range, so each range shows a different but stable shape. On "simulate update", increment a global tick counter and regenerate with seed = base + tick? That would change the whole shape — jittery. Better: keep a rolling buffer: initial 60 points from seeded PRNG; on simulate, push a new point computed from the last point + deterministic delta (from a pre-computed delta array indexed by tick). Deterministic and smooth. Time range only changes axis labels and maybe the number of points shown (slice the last N). Let me do: buffer 96 points; 1H shows last 60, 6H shows last 72, 24H shows last 84, 7D shows all 96. X labels computed from span.

Chart implementation: SVG. Build with JS: compute path from data, gridlines, Y ticks (4-5), X ticks (5-6), 3 polylines/paths, hover: mousemove → find nearest index → crosshair line + circles + tooltip div. Legend toggles visibility (aria-pressed). Current point highlight: last point with a pulsing dot (respect reduced motion).

KPI sparklines: small SVG polylines, deterministic from the same PRNG.

Orbit panel: SVG with Earth at center (or offset), Moon orbit (small circle), Asteria-7 orbit (larger ellipse), and a third orbit (e.g., "Relay orbit" or heliocentric?). Requirement: "Earth, Moon, Asteria-7 与三条轨道" — Earth, Moon, Asteria-7 and 3 orbits. So: Moon orbit around Earth, Asteria-7 orbit around Earth (or heliocentric?), and a third — maybe a "Lagrange relay" orbit or an elliptical transfer. Let me draw: Earth at center, Moon orbit (r=60), Asteria-7 elliptical orbit (rx=150, ry=110, rotated), and a dashed outer orbit "Relay HALO" (r=200). Moon and Asteria-7 as labeled dots. Zoom: scale transform on a <g> with transform-origin center; +/- buttons change scale factor (0.6–2.4), Reset returns to 1. Buttons actually change the drawing scale — yes, via transform.

Positions: deterministic angles (fixed). Maybe animate slow orbit? Reduced motion: no animation. I can add a subtle CSS rotation animation on the orbit group... but rotating the ellipse group would rotate the ellipse shape too. I can animate the probe dot along the orbit with JS requestAnimationFrame at a slow rate, disabled under reduced motion. That's a nice touch. Keep it simple: rAF updates the dot position along the ellipse; deterministic start angle. Under reduced motion, static.

Table: render rows from data array. Search input filters name/model/operator. Status filter: select or segmented chips (All, Nominal, Degraded, Critical, Offline). Sort: click header toggles asc/desc, aria-sort. Pagination: "show more" — show 6, button loads +4? Or page size 8 with prev/next. Let me do: page size 6, "Show more" appends next page (simpler and matches "分页或显示更多"). Actually with 10 records, page size 6 → 2 pages. Show more button with count. Persist filters (search, status, sort) to localStorage.

Row click → drawer. Drawer: probe name, status chip, key data grid (distance, signal, temp, battery, last contact, operator, model, id), mini sparkline, recent event timeline (3-4 items per probe, deterministic), 3 action buttons: "Ping probe" (toast), "Schedule downlink" (confirm modal → toast), "Isolate subsystem" (confirm modal with warning style → toast). Focus management: on open, focus the close button; on close, return focus to the row. Escape closes.

Event stream: list with severity icon + color + text (not color-only: icon shape + text label). Filter chips All/Critical/Warning/Info. Mark read: button per event (check icon) toggles read state (dimmed, "read" label). Persist read state? Not required but nice; persist to localStorage. Unread count feeds the notification badge.

Notifications popover: list of recent events (top 4), "Mark all read" button, badge count = unread events. Live update: when events are marked read in the stream, badge updates.

User menu: Profile, Preferences, Sign out. Outside click closes. Sign out → confirm modal? Or just a toast "Signed out (demo)". Let me do a toast. Preferences → toast or open a small settings? Keep it as a toast "Preferences panel is a stub in this demo" — hmm, better: Preferences toggles... let me just do a toast. Actually to be safe, "Preferences" can open a small modal with a few toggles (e.g., "Compact density", "Show grid texture")? That's extra. Let me keep it as a toast to limit scope, but the requirement says all buttons should be demoable... a toast is a demo. OK.

Command palette: overlay with input, list of commands: nav items (7), probes (10, "Open Vega (AST-7/01)"), actions (Simulate telemetry update, Toggle theme, Mark all events read, Collapse sidebar). Filter by query, arrow keys move active, Enter executes, Escape closes. Focus input on open; restore focus on close.

Simulate telemetry update button: where? In the Overview header area ("Simulate update" button) and also in the command palette. On click: tick++, advance the series buffer, update KPI values (deterministic delta), update table signal/battery/temp slightly (deterministic per tick), update last sync time to current UTC, toast "Telemetry frame #N received". KPI deltas recompute.

Skeleton: on load, show skeleton blocks in the main area for ~500ms, then fade in content. Reduced motion: skip (immediate). Implement with a class on body; skeleton elements are placeholders with shimmer (animation disabled under reduced motion). After 500ms (or 0), remove skeleton and render. Actually simpler: render content immediately but overlay a skeleton? Cleaner: main content sections have a `data-skeleton` state — show skeleton divs, then swap. Let me do: on DOMContentLoaded, if not reduced motion, add `is-loading` class to body; CSS shows skeleton shimmer on `.skel` elements that exist in the markup in place of dynamic content; after 500ms, JS renders real content and removes the class. To keep DOM maintainable, dynamic containers (KPI grid, table body, events, kanban) are filled by JS; during loading, they contain skeleton markup (a few .skel divs). After timeout, JS fills real data. That works.

Persistence keys (namespaced): `nmc.theme`, `nmc.sidebar` (collapsed bool), `nmc.filters` (search/status/sort), `nmc.kanban` (column assignments), `nmc.eventsRead` (ids), `nmc.range` (time range).

Accessibility:
- Focus-visible styles: 2px accent outline with offset.
- aria-label on icon buttons.
- aria-expanded on disclosure buttons (sidebar collapse, notifications, user menu, mobile menu).
- aria-live="polite" on toast container and last sync.
- role="dialog" aria-modal on drawer, palette, modal.
